run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:46:52Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend-proxy RequestErrorRate warning is explained by real 5xx/timeout responses at the proxy, not by a proxy-side fault: the proxy's own access log records 'POST /api/checkout' returning 504 UT response_timeout at its 15 s limit, and a full trace shows that request spending ~89 s in frontend -> checkout PlaceOrder, whose Kafka producer span 'orders publish' ended in error 'circuit breaker is open'. The checkout container concurrently logs 'Failed to produce message to topic orders: circuit breaker is open' and a metadata fetch 'read tcp ...->100.71.78.255:9092: i/o timeout' toward Kafka. Chaos-mesh events show a Schedule named otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition spawning NetworkChaos objects every minute that apply network chaos to otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l and both kafka pods and then recover them, which fits the client-side Kafka i/o timeouts; however the events view only returns those runs from 02:06:21Z onward, after the alert's 01:46:52Z start, so the fault's activity before that is unobserved and the cause attribution stays a hypothesis. Separately, the ad pod was OOMKilled at 02:04:33Z and ad/frontend recorded GetAds and /api/data errors from about 02:00, with one proxy 'GET /api/data' 500 seen; that can only contribute after ~02:00 and cannot explain the alert onset. All otel-demo deployments were fully ready and all pods except ad had zero restarts, so a workload outage is not supported.

claims.text: frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR carried a 20-minute increase of 125.39 at 01:50:00Z, 435.43 at 02:00:00Z, 803.08 at 02:10:00Z, 989.74 at 02:15:00Z and 922.76 at 02:20:00Z (sampled 01:50-02:20).

The frontend-proxy error spans returned for the window are 'ingress' spans with error=true, http.status_code=504 and durations about 15,000,000 us (15 s), plus child 'router frontend egress' spans with error='true' and http.status_code=0.

frontend-proxy's access log records 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1' 504 UT response_timeout at 02:09:33Z, 02:14:55Z, 02:14:59Z, 02:15:00Z, 02:15:01Z, 02:15:02Z, 02:15:04Z, 02:15:10Z and 02:15:11Z, and one 'GET /api/data?contextKeys=binoculars HTTP/1.1' 500 via_upstream at 02:09:34Z, while sibling requests (e.g. GET /api/cart, GET /api/products/...) returned 200.

Trace f18dd56ad5afb108674a31c6c7770ed1 shows the call path load-generator POST -> frontend-proxy ingress (504, 15.0 s) -> frontend 'POST /api/checkout' (89.09 s) -> checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (89.08 s) -> checkout span 'orders publish' (88.87 s, error=true, otel.status_description='circuit breaker is open').

The checkout container logs 'Failed to write message: kafka: Failed to produce message to topic orders: circuit breaker is open' at 01:46:56Z-01:47:23Z, at 01:49:09Z and at 02:14:19Z, and 'client/metadata got error from broker 1 while fetching metadata: read tcp 100.96.1.134:53048->100.71.78.255:9092: i/o timeout' at 02:15:00Z.

The checkout span 'orders publish' (span_kind SPAN_KIND_PRODUCER) has only a STATUS_CODE_ERROR series, with 2-minute increases of 38.67 at 01:49, 37.33 at 01:51, 36.0 at 01:53, 41.33 at 01:55, 37.33 at 01:59, 30.67 in the 02:01-02:03 buckets, 36.0 at 02:05, 30.67 at 02:07, 34.67 at 02:09 and 0 in the 02:11-02:17 buckets.

Chaos-mesh events show NetworkChaos objects named otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition-* each recording 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l', '... for otel-demo/kafka-ff7884766-xclnk' and '... for otel-demo/kafka-ff7884766-skk8d', followed by TimeUp and 'Successfully recover chaos' for the same three pods, and 51 PodNetworkChaos 'Updated' events name exactly those three pods in namespace otel-demo.

Events of kind Schedule in namespace chaos-mesh show object otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition spawning a new NetworkChaos object every minute from 02:06:21Z through 02:14:21Z (e.g. 'Create new object: otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition-fkbbr' at 02:06:21Z).

Pod ad-554b849958-4chjq has restartCount 1 with lastState terminated reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 02:04:33Z; it is otherwise Running and ready, and its Pod events (Pulled/Created/Started) carry lastTimestamp 02:04:33Z.

The ad service's own spans record errors: 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean' STATUS_CODE_ERROR 38.86 per 10 m in the 02:20 bucket and 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 1.05 in the 02:10 bucket.

The frontend service's own spans record identical error counts for 'GET /api/data', 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds': 231.58 per 10 m in the 02:10 bucket and 101.34 in the 02:20 bucket, with tcp.connect 13.68 and 2.11 in the same buckets.
The checkout service's own error-span increase was 130.0, 113.75, 123.33, 114.10, 146.67 and 138.89 per 5 m at the sampled instants 01:51:52Z through 02:16:52Z.
Accounting, payment and recommendation had 0 error-span increase and fraud-detection 0 except 1.11 in two 5-minute buckets, at each sampled instant from 01:51:52Z to 02:16:52Z.

All 21 otel-demo deployments report desired == available == ready replicas (checkout 1/1/1, kafka 2/2/2, frontend-proxy 1/1/1, ad 1/1/1, frontend 1/1/1), and all 22 otel-demo pods are Running and ready with restartCount 0 except ad-554b849958-4chjq (1).

Primary explanation: the proxy's 504s on /api/checkout are a downstream symptom - checkout's Kafka produce attempt occupies ~89 s and ends with 'circuit breaker is open' after Kafka metadata fetches time out at the TCP level, which exceeds frontend-proxy's 15 s route timeout and yields the 504 UT response_timeout entries that drive the frontend-proxy error-rate alert.

The Kafka produce failures are most plausibly caused by the recurring network partition injected by chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition in namespace chaos-mesh, whose NetworkChaos children are applied to the checkout pod and both kafka pods and recovered about 55 s later each minute, matching the observed client-side i/o timeouts while the kafka brokers themselves stay ready.

A second, independent contributor appears after ~02:00: ad was OOMKilled and restarted at 02:04:33Z, ad recorded flagd ResolveBoolean errors, frontend recorded matching GetAds and /api/data error counts, and the proxy logged a 'GET /api/data' 500; this could add proxy errors for non-checkout requests but cannot explain the alert's 01:46:52Z onset.

A remaining unresolved candidate: the kafka broker logs periodic '[ControllerApis nodeId=1] Unexpected error handling request ... AssignReplicasToDirsRequestData' lines about every 10 s and repeated '[QuorumController id=1] CreateTopics ... TOPIC_ALREADY_EXISTS' for __consumer_offsets; no evidence ties these broker-side messages to checkout's TCP i/o timeout, so broker-internal trouble is neither confirmed as a cause nor excluded.

Kafka broker unavailability caused by pod failure is not supported: the kafka deployment reports 2 desired / 2 available / 2 ready, both kafka-ff7884766-xclnk and kafka-ff7884766-skk8d are Running and ready with restartCount 0, and their containers are actively logging broker activity.

A frontend-proxy-originated fault is not supported: the same proxy pod served other paths with 200 (GET /api/cart, GET /api/products/..., GET /api/recommendations) at the same time it returned 504 on /api/checkout, and the trace shows the frontend/checkout chain consuming ~89 s while the proxy cut the request at 15 s.

A rollout or workload restart as the trigger at alert onset is not supported: all otel-demo pods started at 01:34:53Z-01:36:45Z, the only container restart is the ad container at 02:04:33Z (after the 01:46:52Z alert start), and all deployments report full ready replicas.

The NetworkChaos/Schedule events that name checkout and kafka span only 02:06:21Z-02:14:21Z (the events view's source_start_at is 02:06:21Z), later than the alert's 01:46:52Z start; the earliest checkout circuit-breaker log line I could observe is 01:46:56Z, so the observed chaos runs do not themselves cover the alert onset.

gaps: The alerting rule itself is unknown: list_prometheus_rules returned no_data for rule_name RequestErrorRate (ff5e1c04-f0c5-47c9-ab97-f13417916061-t0:1c3740ac-2e77-4b9f-88a1-dfe7b07746bf), for rule_group RequestErrorRate (05ffbb91-9191-4150-b622-e71f656abe53-t0:06fceec7-02ac-4b95-97c0-d072841c92f3) and for type=alert (7fbd603e-aff9-4327-8ba0-ce45a5947b08-t1:34205381-21f1-47f6-8fdd-fa4f3ad06ec8), so the expression, threshold and for-duration behind 'current: 1.6' could not be read or recomputed.

The frontend-proxy error-span series available in this view begin at 01:50:00Z, after the alert start of 01:46:52Z, so there is no pre-alert baseline; the deviation point and any earlier error rate are unknown, and no latency trend comparison is possible.

chaos-mesh Schedule and NetworkChaos specs can only be seen through events in this Run; the schedule's targets, direction, duration, start time and whether it was active before 02:06:21Z are unknown, and event retention in the returned view starts at 02:06:21Z.

The checkout container's retained log lines postdate the 01:20Z-01:42Z queries (a fetch over 00:46:52Z-01:20:00Z returned no_data: 0e394419-7886-42bf-a600-5ec2c962b893-t0:0143d241-7149-4371-9722-42157d668fd9), so when the Kafka produce failures actually began before ~01:46Z is unobserved.

The tail of the checkout 'orders publish' error series (0 per 2 m in the 02:11-02:17 buckets) conflicts with 504s logged at 02:14:55Z-02:15:11Z and with a 243.85 per-10 m increase in the 02:20 bucket; the metric views also had different data_as_of values (02:17 vs 02:20), so the end or recovery of the checkout-to-Kafka failure is unresolved.

The networkpolicies query for namespace otel-demo returned no_data (151b767e-ff30-4f5f-9a88-bb11d5b41eaa-t0:4646a1cb-8cfe-419e-9dce-ad74fa970dde), so I cannot confirm whether any Kubernetes NetworkPolicy participates in the checkout-to-Kafka connectivity problem.
No previous-container logs were available for the ad container (the pod reported no previous instance), so why ad exceeded its memory limit and was OOMKilled at 02:04:33Z could not be determined.

Secrets cannot be read, and no configuration object was inspected that explains the failures; change history is not integrated in this Run, so no deployment, ConfigMap or chaos-schedule change record is available for the window.
next_steps: Read the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition and its NetworkChaos children (spec target selectors, direction, duration, schedule, history) to confirm whether the partition was active at 01:46:52Z and to correlate apply/recover times with per-minute proxy errors.
Retrieve the RequestErrorRate alerting rule definition from the alerting configuration/Alertmanager source and evaluate it over a pre-incident baseline (before 01:46:52Z).
Review the ad container's memory request/limit and OOM behaviour, and confirm whether ad's 02:04:33Z restart measurably increased /api/data 5xx responses at the proxy.
Inspect KRaft controller/broker health on kafka-ff7884766-xclnk and kafka-ff7884766-skk8d for the repeated AssignReplicasToDirsRequestData errors and __consumer_offsets CreateTopics loop.
Compare checkout-to-Kafka connectivity during a recovered interval versus an applied-chaos interval to test whether produce errors track the NetworkChaos windows.
